newsitem.title: USA: Union, N.J., incinerator working on fees -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Union, N.J., incinerator working on fees -- paper.

text.p: Union County Utilities Authority in New Jersey is considering a plan to lower its tipping fees by forming a consortium of communities willing to guarantee waste streams, the Star Ledger reported Sunday.
The $283 million facility is trying to deal with recent court decisions invalidating the state's current system of guaranteeing a steady stream of waste to particular facilities.
That system enabled facilities to sell bonds with the expectation that high tipping fees would support the debt.

But the court rulings mean the facilities will have to compete for trash in a competitive market, rather than relying on waste deliveries mandated by law. At $83.05 per ton for disposal, the Union incinerator is one of the highest-priced facilities in the state, the newspaper said, and many waste generators will turn to cheaper facilities when the law permits.
An appeals court decision earlier this month shortened the deadline by which the facilities need to find an alternative, probably to October.
The newspaper also said the Union facility is negotiating with Ogden Martin Systems of Union Inc., the operator of the incinerator, to renegotiate the terms of the contract.
In the secondary market Monday, a block of the authority's solid waste 7.10s of 2006 were being offered at 103. Kenny Evaluation Services Inc. priced the bonds at the close Friday at 100.15.
A second block of the authority's 7.20s of 2014 were offered at 102. Kenny priced those bonds Friday at 100.001.
The bonds are rated BB by both Standard & Poor's Corp. and Fitch Investors Service Inc., and are not rated by Moody's Investors Service Inc.
